strategy.reason: All 14 recorded experiments across cycles BOOTSTRAP through cycle 5 failed for purely infrastructural reasons: C001 missing AlgorithmAgent.run() positional args, C002_H01/H02 violating the latent_dim contract, C002_H03 reaching into final-test inside representation.normalization (and then crashing on a GBK UnicodeEncodeError), and C003, C004, and the cycle-5 H1/H2/H3 hypotheses all crashing at import time because ContractValidationError and AlgorithmContractError are not exported from runtime.algorithm_contract. Zero scientific mechanisms have been falsified. The strategy therefore remains parallel exploration, but the new three hypotheses must (a) commit to mechanisms that none of the prior 14 hypotheses tested and (b) be discriminable from one another. The selected mechanisms are: (i) Lie-group / SO(n)-equivariant latent dynamics — tests whether geometric symmetry is an inductive bias, distinct from every unconstrained linear/polynomial/SINDy/Koopman attempt; (ii) function-space operator in an RKHS with an operator-valued kernel — tests whether the latent operator is smoother than any finite matrix can represent, distinct from the parameter-switched Koopman of C002_H02; (iii) compositional graph-structured latent dynamics with learned block partition and sparse inter-block coupling — tests whether the 52D operator has a hierarchical block-banded structure, distinct from the energy-band-structured C003_H02 and the regime-switched BOOTSTRAP_H1. None of these is a hyperparameter retune of a previously falsified mechanism; each introduces a new mathematical object (equivariance constraint, operator-valued kernel, graph-structured operator) and each carries a built-in discrimination signature.

hypotheses.name: Lie-group equivariant latent dynamics: SO(n) / O(d) symmetry as an inductive bias on the 52D operator
hypotheses.scientific_question: Do the 52D latent coordinates carry a geometric (rotational / reflectional / permutation) symmetry such that the latent dynamics commutes with a nontrivial Lie-group action on R^52, and would enforcing that equivariance as an inductive bias improve predictive accuracy and parameter efficiency on development_validation?
hypotheses.mechanism: Replace the unconstrained linear map x_{t+1} = A x_t (C001-H01, C003-H01/H02/H03, BOOTSTRAP_H1) or unconstrained polynomial map (C002-H03) by a group-equivariant dynamics on R^52. The operator is restricted to the commutant algebra of a chosen compact Lie group G acting on R^52; for G = O(52) this collapses to the diagonal scaling map x_{t+1,i} = lambda_i x_{t,i}, for G = SO(2) acting as independent rotations on disjoint 2-planes the operator is block-diagonal with 26 coupled 2x2 rotation-shear blocks, and for a learned group generated by a small set of commuting skew-symmetric matrices the dynamics decomposes into the corresponding isotypic components. The training objective is min_theta E[||x_{t+1} - f_theta(x_t)||^2] subject to f_theta o rho(g) = rho(g) o f_theta for all g in G, where rho is the chosen representation.
hypotheses.mathematical_form: f_theta(x) = sum_{ell in Irreps(G)} W_ell * phi_ell(x) where phi_ell maps the ell-th isotypic component of R^52 to itself via an equivariant polynomial / MLP. For G = O(52): f_theta(x)_i = sigma(a_i + b_i x_i) (diagonal). For G = SO(2) acting on 26 independent 2-planes: f_theta((u_k, v_k)) = R(theta_k) * MLP_k(u_k, v_k) where R is a 2x2 rotation parameterized per plane. For a learned G generated by a single skew-symmetric S in so(52): f_theta(x) = exp(S t) * x + correction where the correction lies in the commutant of exp(S t). Closed-form dimension reduction: parameter count drops from 52^2 = 2704 (unconstrained linear) to O(52) (O(52)) or 26*4 = 104 (SO(2)) or O(52*rank(G)) (learned S).
hypotheses.motivation: Fluid-flow reduced-order models (ROM) derived from PDEs with continuous symmetries (Galilean invariance, rotation, reflection, permutation of identical bodies) must commute with those symmetries at the discrete level. Prior hypotheses C001-H01, C002-H02, C003-H01/H02/H03, and BOOTSTRAP_H1 all use unconstrained operators that can only learn symmetry from data and are free to break it. The scientific question of H1 is whether the symmetry is actually present in the 52D latent coordinates and whether enforcing it as a constraint improves generalization. This is a qualitatively different claim: not 'what is the best linear/polynomial/nonlinear form' but 'does the dynamics respect a hidden symmetry of the inertial manifold?'
hypotheses.explanation_of_previous_failure: None of the 14 prior experiments tested equivariance: BOOTSTRAP_H1 tested regime-switching, C001-H01 tested delay-coordinates, C001-H02 tested divergence-free coordinates (a different physical constraint), C001-H03 tested slow/fast decomposition, C002-H01 tested symplectic structure, C002-H02 tested exogenous-parameter conditioning, C002-H03 tested SINDy with closure, C003-H01 tested Bayesian shrinkage, C003-H02 tested energy-band sparsity, C003-H03 tested energy-tail residual, C004-H01 tested non-modal growth, C004-H02 tested information-theoretic nonlinearity, C004-H03 tested recurrence-density heterogeneity, H1 (cycle 5) tested Itô SDE, H2 (cycle 5) tested port-Hamiltonian, H3 (cycle 5) tested diffusion-map. The 14 mechanisms span linear, polynomial, stochastic, dissipative, multi-scale, but none imposes a Lie-group symmetry constraint. H1 is therefore not a retried version of any prior hypothesis; it asks a different scientific question (is the dynamics equivariant?) and uses a different mathematical object (the commutant algebra of a Lie group representation).
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: (a) On held-out trajectories that are exact images of training trajectories under a learned G-action, H1 should achieve error statistically indistinguishable from non-imaged held-out error, while an unconstrained linear baseline should be measurably worse. (b) The learned operator, when projected onto the isotypic decomposition of G, should have near-zero off-block norm; this is a falsifiable quantitative signature. (c) At matched parameter count, H1 should achieve lower one-step RMSE than unconstrained linear, and lower n-step rollout error at horizon 50 on development_validation.
minimum_experiment: Use development_train only. Fit the 52D POD / autoencoder encoder once and freeze it; do not retrain the encoder inside H1.

Choose the group G as SO(2) acting on 26 disjoint 2-planes of the 52D latent space (the most defensible default; O(52) and a learned one-parameter subgroup are control variants run only if SO(2) is informative).
Train H1 on development_train with equivariant layers; evaluate on development_validation only.

Report: one-step RMSE on development_validation; n-step rollout RMSE at horizons {1, 5, 10, 25, 50}; parameter count; off-block / in-block Frobenius norm ratio of the learned linearized operator; symmetry-violation diagnostic on rotated held-out trajectories (constructed by applying a known SO(2) action in the original state space, encoding, and re-running).
Compare to an unconstrained linear baseline (single 52x52 matrix) fit on the same development_train with identical encoder and identical loss, evaluated on the identical development_validation split.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_true: One-step RMSE on development_validation is at least 10% lower than the unconstrained linear baseline at equal or lower parameter count. The off-block / in-block norm ratio is below 0.15. The symmetry-violation diagnostic on rotated held-out trajectories shows H1's error does not increase under rotation while the baseline's error does. Long-horizon rollout error grows sublinearly with horizon up to 50.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_false: One-step RMSE is not significantly different from unconstrained linear (or is worse). Off-block / in-block norm ratio is comparable to a randomly initialized equivariant network. Rotating held-out trajectories degrades H1's performance similarly to the baseline, indicating the latent space does not carry the assumed symmetry. The equivariance constraint is binding (training loss increases when enforced) and does not translate to held-out improvement.
risks: The 52D latent basis may not respect any natural Lie-group action; the symmetry hypothesis may be vacuous for this dataset, in which case H1 reduces to a restricted-capacity linear model.

The choice of group G (SO(2) vs O(52) vs learned) introduces a modeling choice that could mask or fabricate the equivariance signal; the experiment must commit to one default and treat the others as controls.
Equivariant layers are 2-5x slower per step than dense linear maps, so the development_train fitting budget may need to be extended.

If the 52D POD basis is itself not rotation-aligned (e.g., it is defined by a snapshot SVD whose modes are not symmetry-adapted), the equivariance signal will be diluted and H1 will underperform despite underlying physical symmetry; this confound must be acknowledged in the writeup.
hypotheses.relation_to_existing_methods: H1 differs from C002-H02 (exogenous-parameter-conditioned local Koopman) because C002-H02 conditions on a scalar parameter and learns a different linear map per regime, whereas H1 conditions on a hidden group action and learns a single map constrained to commute with that action. H1 differs from C002-H01 (symplectic / energy-preserving) because symplecticity is a property of Hamiltonian flows, not a symmetry constraint; symplectic structure is compatible with equivariance but is neither necessary nor sufficient. H1 differs from C001-H02 (divergence-free coordinates), which imposes a pointwise incompressibility constraint on the encoder, not an equivariance constraint on the dynamics. E(3)-equivariant graph networks and equivariant MLPs for PDEs (e.g., neural SPH, E(n)-equivariant ResNets) exist in the literature, but their application as a hard symmetry constraint on a 52D POD-like latent operator for this benchmark is, to my knowledge, not previously reported.

hypotheses.name: Function-space latent operator in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space: operator-valued Matérn kernel fit by sparse Gaussian process
hypotheses.scientific_question: Is the latent operator x -> x_{t+1} a smooth element of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), and is the smoothness (Matérn nu) class better modeled in infinite-dimensional function space than as a finite 52x52 matrix?
hypotheses.mechanism: Replace the finite linear operator A in R^{52x52} (used in C001-H01, C003-H01/H02/H03, BOOTSTRAP_H1, C002-H02's local linear pieces, etc.) by a vector-valued function T: R^52 -> R^52 drawn from an RKHS with an operator-valued Matérn kernel K: R^52 x R^52 -> R^{52x52}. The kernel enforces that the operator is a function of bounded variation / k-times differentiable (controlled by Matérn nu), and the operator is fit to data via sparse variational GP regression with M << N inducing points chosen by K-means in the latent space. This is a function-space hypothesis: the claim is not 'the operator is a matrix' (which is the implicit claim of every prior linear hypothesis) but 'the operator is a function whose regularity is captured by a kernel.'
hypotheses.mathematical_form: T(x) ~ GP(0, K) with K(x, x') = diag_i [ k_nu_i, l_i(x, x') ] + cross-coupling K_off(x, x'), where k_nu is the Matérn kernel with smoothness nu and lengthscale l. Fit: maximize the sparse variational ELBO with M = 200 inducing points, kernel hyperparameters {nu_i, l_i} learned per output dimension. One-step prediction: x_{t+1} = T(x_t). The inducing point locations Z = {z_m} in R^52 and the inducing values U = {u_m} in R^52 are the learned parameters. Predictive posterior: p(x_{t+1} | x_t) = N(mu(x_t), Sigma(x_t)) with mu(x_t) = k_xZ K_ZZ^{-1} U, k_xZ the kernel vector between x_t and Z, and K_ZZ the M x M kernel matrix. The hypothesis is that this GP-form posterior, fit on development_train, yields better calibrated uncertainty and lower one-step error on development_validation than a finite 52x52 matrix fit by least squares on the same development_train.
hypotheses.motivation: Every prior linear hypothesis (C001, C003, BOOTSTRAP, and the linear parts of C002) treats the latent operator as a member of a 2704-dimensional Euclidean space. A Matérn-kernel GP operator lives in a function space whose complexity is controlled by the kernel smoothness and the number of inducing points; the function-space perspective allows the operator to be nearly identity in low-data regions and strongly nonlinear in data-rich regions, and gives well-calibrated predictive uncertainty. The scientific question is whether the latent operator's true regularity is closer to that of a smooth (nu >= 1) or rough (nu = 1/2) function, and whether function-space regularization (implicit in the kernel) is the right inductive bias. This is qualitatively different from a parametric matrix hypothesis: changing nu changes the effective hypothesis class without changing the parametric form of A.
hypotheses.explanation_of_previous_failure: C002-H02 used local linear Koopman with parameter conditioning; that is a piecewise-linear model with finite-dimensional pieces, not a function-space model. C003-H01 used Bayesian hierarchical shrinkage on a single 52x52 matrix, which is a prior on a finite-dimensional parameter vector, not a function-space smoothness prior. C002-H03 used SINDy polynomial regression with a learned closure residual, which is a sparse polynomial model, not a kernel model. C003-H02 used a sparsity prior on a single matrix; C003-H03 used a low-rank plus residual decomposition of a single matrix. None of these places the operator in an RKHS. H2 is therefore not a retried variant of any prior linear hypothesis with a different sparsity pattern or shrinkage weight; it is a different mathematical object (an operator-valued random function) with a different inductive bias (kernel smoothness) and a different inference scheme (sparse variational GP).
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: (a) If the true latent operator is Matérn-smooth, the marginal log-likelihood on development_validation under H2 should exceed that of a single-matrix linear model with a comparable parameter budget, and the calibrated coverage of the predictive 90% interval should be closer to 90%. (b) Learning the Matérn nu via type-II maximum likelihood should converge to nu >= 1 if the operator is smooth and to nu ~ 1/2 if the operator is rough; this learned nu is a falsifiable signature. (c) One-step RMSE on development_validation should be at or below the unconstrained linear baseline, especially in low-data regions of the latent space. (d) Predictive variance should correlate with development_validation one-step error (calibration), which a finite matrix cannot express.
minimum_experiment: Use development_train only. Freeze the 52D encoder. Do not retrain the encoder inside H2.
Fit H2 with M = 200 inducing points chosen by K-means on the development_train latent states, kernel = operator-valued Matérn with diagonal form plus a low-rank cross-coupling term of rank 8.
Fit a baseline: unconstrained 52x52 linear operator fit by ridge regression on the same development_train with the same encoder.
Evaluate both on development_validation only.

Report: one-step RMSE; marginal log-likelihood on development_validation; 90% predictive interval coverage; learned Matérn nu; predictive variance calibration curve (predicted std vs empirical one-step error); wall-clock fit time.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_true: Marginal log-likelihood on development_validation is higher than the linear baseline. 90% predictive interval coverage is in [85%, 95%]. Learned Matérn nu converges to nu >= 1. Predictive variance correlates with one-step error (Spearman rho > 0.4). One-step RMSE is at or below the linear baseline, with the largest gains in sparsely sampled regions of the latent space.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_false: Marginal log-likelihood is not higher than the linear baseline. Learned nu collapses to 1/2 (the roughest admissible value) and predictive variance is essentially flat. Predictive variance does not correlate with error. One-step RMSE is not significantly different from the linear baseline. The kernel smoothness prior is not the right inductive bias for this problem.
risks: Sparse GP fit with M=200 inducing points is computationally heavier than a single matrix solve; fitting may exceed the development_train budget and require mini-batch variational GP or FITC.
Choice of kernel (Matérn vs RBF vs rational quadratic) introduces a modeling decision; the experiment must commit to Matérn and treat RBF as a control.

If the latent operator is genuinely non-smooth (e.g., discontinuous at regime boundaries as suggested by BOOTSTRAP_H1's inconclusive regime-switching signal), the kernel smoothness prior is the wrong inductive bias and H2 will underperform.
Cross-coupling between output dimensions is hard to learn with a small number of inducing points; a diagonal-only kernel is a simpler fallback that may underfit.
Type-II maximum likelihood for nu is multimodal and can be unstable; the experiment should report the local optimum reached and check sensitivity.
hypotheses.relation_to_existing_methods: H2 differs from C002-H02 (local Koopman) because C002-H02 is a piecewise-linear mixture-of-experts model, whereas H2 is a single global GP operator with kernel smoothness. H2 differs from C003-H01 (Bayesian hierarchical shrinkage) because the prior in C003-H01 is on a finite-dimensional matrix, whereas the prior in H2 is a kernel that places the operator in an infinite-dimensional function space. H2 differs from C002-H03 (SINDy + closure) because SINDy uses a polynomial library and H2 uses a kernel. Sparse variational GPs for vector-valued outputs (Cheng et al. 2021, Dutordoir et al. 2021) and operator-valued kernels (Alvarez et al. 2012) are established; their application to a 52D POD-like latent ROM is, to my knowledge, novel and is a direct test of the function-space smoothness hypothesis.

hypotheses.name: Compositional graph-structured latent dynamics: learned block partition with sparse inter-block coupling
hypotheses.scientific_question: Does the 52D latent operator have a hierarchical compositional structure, in which the 52 latent coordinates partition into a small number of interacting groups (blocks) with strong intra-block dynamics and weak, sparse inter-block coupling, and is such a block-banded structure a better inductive bias than the fully coupled 52x52 matrix?
hypotheses.mechanism: Replace the dense 52x52 linear operator (used in C001, C003, BOOTSTRAP, C002-H02's local pieces) by a structured operator of the form A = D + B, where D is a block-diagonal matrix with K blocks (K learned, with K in {2, 4, 8, 13, 26} as the candidate set) and B is a sparse inter-block coupling matrix whose support is chosen by a learned stochastic block model (SBM) on the K blocks. The block assignment z_i in {1, ..., K} for each latent coordinate i is jointly learned with the operator via a Gumbel-softmax relaxation. Within each block k, the dynamics is a small d_k x d_k matrix (d_k = 52 / K approximately). Between blocks, the dynamics is a sparse set of inter-block matrices W_{kk'} with low rank (rank <= 2). The hypothesis is that the 52 latent coordinates are not fully coupled but admit a low-bandwidth interaction structure, and that this compositional prior is the right inductive bias.
hypotheses.mathematical_form: x = (x_1, ..., x_K) with x_k in R^{d_k}, sum d_k = 52. Dynamics: x_{k, t+1} = A_k x_{k, t} + sum_{k' in N(k)} W_{k, k'} x_{k', t}, where N(k) is the neighborhood of block k in the SBM adjacency graph and W_{k, k'} is a low-rank inter-block matrix of rank r <= 2. The block assignment p(z_i = k) is parameterized by a K x 52 softmax matrix with Gumbel-softmax temperature annealed from 1.0 to 0.1. The SBM adjacency probabilities are parameterized by a K x K matrix P_knn with row-stochastic normalization, learned jointly. Total parameter count: sum_k d_k^2 + sum_{k, k' in E} r * (d_k + d_{k'}) + K * 52, where E is the SBM edge set. For K=4, d_k=13, r=2, |E|=4 (sparse 4-cycle), this is 4*169 + 4*2*(13+13) + 4*52 = 676 + 208 + 208 = 1092, less than half of the 2704 parameters of a dense 52x52 matrix.
hypotheses.motivation: A 52D latent space from a snapshot SVD or autoencoder of a fluid flow rarely has uniformly dense coupling between all latent coordinates; physical structure (adjacent spatial modes, velocity-pressure coupling, energy cascade) typically induces a banded or block-banded interaction. Prior hypotheses C003-H02 (POD-energy-band-structured sparse latent linear operator) imposed energy-band sparsity on a single matrix; H3 imposes a different sparsity structure: a learned block partition combined with a learned SBM inter-block graph. C002-H02 (regime-aware Koopman) imposed regime-switching on a single matrix; H3 imposes compositional structure that is time-invariant but hierarchically organized. The scientific question of H3 is whether the 52D operator has a block-banded signature that can be discovered from data and exploited as an inductive bias, yielding a more parameter-efficient and more interpretable model than a fully coupled matrix.
hypotheses.explanation_of_previous_failure: C003-H02 used energy-band sparsity on a single 52x52 matrix; that is a fixed sparsity pattern derived from the energy ordering of the latent basis, not a learned block partition. C003-H01 used a single shrinkage prior on a single matrix, no structure. C003-H03 used a low-rank-plus-residual decomposition of a single matrix; that is a global low-rank structure, not a compositional block structure. BOOTSTRAP_H1 used a regime-dependent family of operators; that is a temporal / regime structure, not a compositional block structure. C002-H02 used parameter-conditioned local linear maps; that is a piecewise-linear structure, not a block-banded structure. None of the 14 prior hypotheses learned a block partition jointly with the operator and a graph on the blocks. H3 is therefore not a retried version of C003-H02 with a different number of energy bands or a different regularization weight; it is a different mathematical object (block-partitioned operator with SBM inter-block graph) with a different inductive bias (compositional sparsity) and a different learning algorithm (joint Gumbel-softmax block assignment + SBM edge learning).
hypotheses.distinguishing_prediction: (a) The learned block partition should be non-trivially aligned with the energy ordering of the latent basis (Spearman correlation between block index and POD energy rank > 0.3) IF energy-band structure is the binding factor; otherwise the block partition should be approximately random, falsifying the energy-band hypothesis. (b) The SBM adjacency matrix should be sparse, with average degree < K/2; if it is dense, the compositional structure is not realized and H3 collapses to a fully coupled model. (c) At matched parameter count, H3 should achieve one-step RMSE on development_validation that is not statistically different from the dense 52x52 linear baseline, and should outperform it at lower parameter counts (e.g., H3 with K=4 should match dense linear at 1092 vs 2704 parameters). (d) The off-block / in-block Frobenius norm ratio of the learned operator should be below 0.2, providing a falsifiable quantitative signature of the compositional structure.
minimum_experiment: Use development_train only. Freeze the 52D encoder. Do not retrain the encoder inside H3.
Train H3 with K in {2, 4, 8, 13, 26} as a hyperparameter sweep on development_train only (no peeking at development_validation during sweep).
Fit baseline: unconstrained 52x52 linear operator fit by ridge regression on the same development_train with the same encoder.
Evaluate both on development_validation only.

Report: one-step RMSE on development_validation as a function of K; n-step rollout RMSE at horizons {1, 5, 10, 25, 50}; parameter count; SBM adjacency matrix; block-energy alignment (Spearman correlation between block index and POD energy rank); off-block / in-block Frobenius norm ratio; block-assignment entropy as a function of Gumbel temperature.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_true: One-step RMSE is not significantly different from the dense linear baseline at K >= 4 and is at most 5% worse. SBM adjacency is sparse (average degree <= K/2). Off-block / in-block norm ratio is below 0.2. Block-energy alignment is non-trivial. Long-horizon rollout error grows sublinearly. The K = 4 model matches the dense linear baseline with less than half the parameters.
hypotheses.expected_observation_if_false: One-step RMSE is significantly worse than the dense linear baseline at all K. SBM adjacency is dense (average degree close to K), indicating the block structure is not realized. Off-block / in-block norm ratio is comparable to a random matrix. Block-energy alignment is statistically indistinguishable from random. The compositional prior is not the right inductive bias; the dynamics is approximately fully coupled.
risks: Joint Gumbel-softmax block assignment and SBM edge learning is non-convex and may converge to different local optima; the experiment must report multiple random restarts and pick the best by development_train log-likelihood, not by development_validation.
The choice of K is a modeling decision; K = 4 and K = 8 are reasonable defaults but the data may favor a different K.
If the latent basis is genuinely fully coupled (no physical block structure), H3 will underperform the dense linear baseline, and the failure mode is informative, not a flaw.
The SBM prior may be too restrictive; a multi-edge-type SBM or a learned nonparametric block model is a more flexible fallback that may be needed in cycle 7 if H3 is informative but underfits.
hypotheses.relation_to_existing_methods: H3 differs from C003-H02 (POD-energy-band sparse) because the sparsity structure is learned (Gumbel-softmax block assignment + SBM), not fixed by the energy ordering of the basis. H3 differs from BOOTSTRAP_H1 (regime-dependent) because H3 is time-invariant block structure, not time-dependent regime switching. H3 differs from C002-H02 (regime-aware Koopman) for the same reason and because H3 is a single global operator, not a mixture of local linear maps. Stochastic block models (Nowicki & Snijders 2001, Peixoto 2014) and graph-structured linear operators (e.g., graph neural network linear layers) are established; their use as a learned compositional prior on a 52D latent ROM is, to my knowledge, novel.

hypothesis.name: Function-space latent operator in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space: operator-valued Matérn kernel fit by sparse Gaussian process
hypothesis.scientific_question: Is the latent operator x -> x_{t+1} a smooth element of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), and is the smoothness (Matérn nu) class better modeled in infinite-dimensional function space than as a finite 52x52 matrix?
hypothesis.mechanism: Replace the finite linear operator A in R^{52x52} (used in C001-H01, C003-H01/H02/H03, BOOTSTRAP_H1, C002-H02's local linear pieces, etc.) by a vector-valued function T: R^52 -> R^52 drawn from an RKHS with an operator-valued Matérn kernel K: R^52 x R^52 -> R^{52x52}. The kernel enforces that the operator is a function of bounded variation / k-times differentiable (controlled by Matérn nu), and the operator is fit to data via sparse variational GP regression with M << N inducing points chosen by K-means in the latent space. This is a function-space hypothesis: the claim is not 'the operator is a matrix' (which is the implicit claim of every prior linear hypothesis) but 'the operator is a function whose regularity is captured by a kernel.'
hypothesis.mathematical_form: T(x) ~ GP(0, K) with K(x, x') = diag_i [ k_nu_i, l_i(x, x') ] + cross-coupling K_off(x, x'), where k_nu is the Matérn kernel with smoothness nu and lengthscale l. Fit: maximize the sparse variational ELBO with M = 200 inducing points, kernel hyperparameters {nu_i, l_i} learned per output dimension. One-step prediction: x_{t+1} = T(x_t). The inducing point locations Z = {z_m} in R^52 and the inducing values U = {u_m} in R^52 are the learned parameters. Predictive posterior: p(x_{t+1} | x_t) = N(mu(x_t), Sigma(x_t)) with mu(x_t) = k_xZ K_ZZ^{-1} U, k_xZ the kernel vector between x_t and Z, and K_ZZ the M x M kernel matrix. The hypothesis is that this GP-form posterior, fit on development_train, yields better calibrated uncertainty and lower one-step error on development_validation than a finite 52x52 matrix fit by least squares on the same development_train.
hypothesis.motivation: Every prior linear hypothesis (C001, C003, BOOTSTRAP, and the linear parts of C002) treats the latent operator as a member of a 2704-dimensional Euclidean space. A Matérn-kernel GP operator lives in a function space whose complexity is controlled by the kernel smoothness and the number of inducing points; the function-space perspective allows the operator to be nearly identity in low-data regions and strongly nonlinear in data-rich regions, and gives well-calibrated predictive uncertainty. The scientific question is whether the latent operator's true regularity is closer to that of a smooth (nu >= 1) or rough (nu = 1/2) function, and whether function-space regularization (implicit in the kernel) is the right inductive bias. This is qualitatively different from a parametric matrix hypothesis: changing nu changes the effective hypothesis class without changing the parametric form of A.
hypothesis.explanation_of_previous_failure: C002-H02 used local linear Koopman with parameter conditioning; that is a piecewise-linear model with finite-dimensional pieces, not a function-space model. C003-H01 used Bayesian hierarchical shrinkage on a single 52x52 matrix, which is a prior on a finite-dimensional parameter vector, not a function-space smoothness prior. C002-H03 used SINDy polynomial regression with a learned closure residual, which is a sparse polynomial model, not a kernel model. C003-H02 used a sparsity prior on a single matrix; C003-H03 used a low-rank plus residual decomposition of a single matrix. None of these places the operator in an RKHS. H2 is therefore not a retried variant of any prior linear hypothesis with a different sparsity pattern or shrinkage weight; it is a different mathematical object (an operator-valued random function) with a different inductive bias (kernel smoothness) and a different inference scheme (sparse variational GP).
hypothesis.distinguishing_prediction: (a) If the true latent operator is Matérn-smooth, the marginal log-likelihood on development_validation under H2 should exceed that of a single-matrix linear model with a comparable parameter budget, and the calibrated coverage of the predictive 90% interval should be closer to 90%. (b) Learning the Matérn nu via type-II maximum likelihood should converge to nu >= 1 if the operator is smooth and to nu ~ 1/2 if the operator is rough; this learned nu is a falsifiable signature. (c) One-step RMSE on development_validation should be at or below the unconstrained linear baseline, especially in low-data regions of the latent space. (d) Predictive variance should correlate with development_validation one-step error (calibration), which a finite matrix cannot express.
minimum_experiment: Use development_train only. Freeze the 52D encoder. Do not retrain the encoder inside H2.
Fit H2 with M = 200 inducing points chosen by K-means on the development_train latent states, kernel = operator-valued Matérn with diagonal form plus a low-rank cross-coupling term of rank 8.
Fit a baseline: unconstrained 52x52 linear operator fit by ridge regression on the same development_train with the same encoder.
Evaluate both on development_validation only.

Report: one-step RMSE; marginal log-likelihood on development_validation; 90% predictive interval coverage; learned Matérn nu; predictive variance calibration curve (predicted std vs empirical one-step error); wall-clock fit time.
hypothesis.expected_observation_if_true: Marginal log-likelihood on development_validation is higher than the linear baseline. 90% predictive interval coverage is in [85%, 95%]. Learned Matérn nu converges to nu >= 1. Predictive variance correlates with one-step error (Spearman rho > 0.4). One-step RMSE is at or below the linear baseline, with the largest gains in sparsely sampled regions of the latent space.
hypothesis.expected_observation_if_false: Marginal log-likelihood is not higher than the linear baseline. Learned nu collapses to 1/2 (the roughest admissible value) and predictive variance is essentially flat. Predictive variance does not correlate with error. One-step RMSE is not significantly different from the linear baseline. The kernel smoothness prior is not the right inductive bias for this problem.
risks: Sparse GP fit with M=200 inducing points is computationally heavier than a single matrix solve; fitting may exceed the development_train budget and require mini-batch variational GP or FITC.
Choice of kernel (Matérn vs RBF vs rational quadratic) introduces a modeling decision; the experiment must commit to Matérn and treat RBF as a control.

If the latent operator is genuinely non-smooth (e.g., discontinuous at regime boundaries as suggested by BOOTSTRAP_H1's inconclusive regime-switching signal), the kernel smoothness prior is the wrong inductive bias and H2 will underperform.
Cross-coupling between output dimensions is hard to learn with a small number of inducing points; a diagonal-only kernel is a simpler fallback that may underfit.
Type-II maximum likelihood for nu is multimodal and can be unstable; the experiment should report the local optimum reached and check sensitivity.
hypothesis.relation_to_existing_methods: H2 differs from C002-H02 (local Koopman) because C002-H02 is a piecewise-linear mixture-of-experts model, whereas H2 is a single global GP operator with kernel smoothness. H2 differs from C003-H01 (Bayesian hierarchical shrinkage) because the prior in C003-H01 is on a finite-dimensional matrix, whereas the prior in H2 is a kernel that places the operator in an infinite-dimensional function space. H2 differs from C002-H03 (SINDy + closure) because SINDy uses a polynomial library and H2 uses a kernel. Sparse variational GPs for vector-valued outputs (Cheng et al. 2021, Dutordoir et al. 2021) and operator-valued kernels (Alvarez et al. 2012) are established; their application to a 52D POD-like latent ROM is, to my knowledge, novel and is a direct test of the function-space smoothness hypothesis.

hypothesis.name: Compositional graph-structured latent dynamics: learned block partition with sparse inter-block coupling
hypothesis.scientific_question: Does the 52D latent operator have a hierarchical compositional structure, in which the 52 latent coordinates partition into a small number of interacting groups (blocks) with strong intra-block dynamics and weak, sparse inter-block coupling, and is such a block-banded structure a better inductive bias than the fully coupled 52x52 matrix?
hypothesis.mechanism: Replace the dense 52x52 linear operator (used in C001, C003, BOOTSTRAP, C002-H02's local pieces) by a structured operator of the form A = D + B, where D is a block-diagonal matrix with K blocks (K learned, with K in {2, 4, 8, 13, 26} as the candidate set) and B is a sparse inter-block coupling matrix whose support is chosen by a learned stochastic block model (SBM) on the K blocks. The block assignment z_i in {1, ..., K} for each latent coordinate i is jointly learned with the operator via a Gumbel-softmax relaxation. Within each block k, the dynamics is a small d_k x d_k matrix (d_k = 52 / K approximately). Between blocks, the dynamics is a sparse set of inter-block matrices W_{kk'} with low rank (rank <= 2). The hypothesis is that the 52 latent coordinates are not fully coupled but admit a low-bandwidth interaction structure, and that this compositional prior is the right inductive bias.
hypothesis.mathematical_form: x = (x_1, ..., x_K) with x_k in R^{d_k}, sum d_k = 52. Dynamics: x_{k, t+1} = A_k x_{k, t} + sum_{k' in N(k)} W_{k, k'} x_{k', t}, where N(k) is the neighborhood of block k in the SBM adjacency graph and W_{k, k'} is a low-rank inter-block matrix of rank r <= 2. The block assignment p(z_i = k) is parameterized by a K x 52 softmax matrix with Gumbel-softmax temperature annealed from 1.0 to 0.1. The SBM adjacency probabilities are parameterized by a K x K matrix P_knn with row-stochastic normalization, learned jointly. Total parameter count: sum_k d_k^2 + sum_{k, k' in E} r * (d_k + d_{k'}) + K * 52, where E is the SBM edge set. For K=4, d_k=13, r=2, |E|=4 (sparse 4-cycle), this is 4*169 + 4*2*(13+13) + 4*52 = 676 + 208 + 208 = 1092, less than half of the 2704 parameters of a dense 52x52 matrix.
hypothesis.motivation: A 52D latent space from a snapshot SVD or autoencoder of a fluid flow rarely has uniformly dense coupling between all latent coordinates; physical structure (adjacent spatial modes, velocity-pressure coupling, energy cascade) typically induces a banded or block-banded interaction. Prior hypotheses C003-H02 (POD-energy-band-structured sparse latent linear operator) imposed energy-band sparsity on a single matrix; H3 imposes a different sparsity structure: a learned block partition combined with a learned SBM inter-block graph. C002-H02 (regime-aware Koopman) imposed regime-switching on a single matrix; H3 imposes compositional structure that is time-invariant but hierarchically organized. The scientific question of H3 is whether the 52D operator has a block-banded signature that can be discovered from data and exploited as an inductive bias, yielding a more parameter-efficient and more interpretable model than a fully coupled matrix.
hypothesis.explanation_of_previous_failure: C003-H02 used energy-band sparsity on a single 52x52 matrix; that is a fixed sparsity pattern derived from the energy ordering of the latent basis, not a learned block partition. C003-H01 used a single shrinkage prior on a single matrix, no structure. C003-H03 used a low-rank-plus-residual decomposition of a single matrix; that is a global low-rank structure, not a compositional block structure. BOOTSTRAP_H1 used a regime-dependent family of operators; that is a temporal / regime structure, not a compositional block structure. C002-H02 used parameter-conditioned local linear maps; that is a piecewise-linear structure, not a block-banded structure. None of the 14 prior hypotheses learned a block partition jointly with the operator and a graph on the blocks. H3 is therefore not a retried version of C003-H02 with a different number of energy bands or a different regularization weight; it is a different mathematical object (block-partitioned operator with SBM inter-block graph) with a different inductive bias (compositional sparsity) and a different learning algorithm (joint Gumbel-softmax block assignment + SBM edge learning).

(b) The SBM adjacency matrix should be sparse, with average degree < K/2; if it is dense, the compositional structure is not realized and H3 collapses to a fully coupled model. hypothesis.expected_observation_if_true: One-step RMSE is not significantly different from the dense linear baseline at K >= 4 and is at most 5% worse. The K = 4 model matches the dense linear baseline with less than half the parameters.
hypothesis.expected_observation_if_false: One-step RMSE is significantly worse than the dense linear baseline at all K. H3 differs from C002-H02 (regime-aware Koopman) for the same reason and because H3 is a single global operator, not a mixture of local linear maps. Stochastic block models (Nowicki & Snijders 2001, Peixoto 2014) and graph-structured linear operators (e.g., graph neural network linear layers) are established; their use as a learned compositional prior on a 52D latent ROM is, to my knowledge, novel.
